---
title: "ci/cd pipelines"
---

## what gets automated?

- **ci, continuous integration:** run checks when proposed code changes are integrated or reviewed
- **continuous delivery:** prepare a validated release that can be deployed after approval
- **continuous deployment:** automatically deploy changes that pass the required gates
- a gate is a condition that must pass before the next stage proceeds; a green ci run means its configured checks passed

## github actions vocabulary

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| term / tool | definition | use case |
|---|---|---|
| github actions | github’s workflow automation service | run checks for a pull request or push |
| workflow | an event-triggered configuration written in yaml | describe the sequence of checks |
| yaml | a structured text format using keys and indentation | configure triggers, jobs, and steps |
| runner | the machine executing a job | provide a clean environment for testing |
| job / step | a group of steps / one command or reusable action | install dependencies, then run tests |
| action | a reusable workflow component | check out code or install a python version |
| permission | access granted to the workflow token | allow reading repository contents for checks |

:::

- `actions/checkout` retrieves repository code and `actions/setup-python` selects the python runtime [setup-python documentation](https://github.com/actions/setup-python)

## a minimal ci template

- place the [exercise files](../../examples/automation-demo.zip) at the root of a dedicated repository; the download includes `.github/workflows/checks.yml`
- this template trains a small synthetic candidate and runs the same tests used locally

```yaml
name: model checks
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - run: python -m pip install -r requirements-test.in
      - run: python run_workflow.py --run-id run-001
      - run: python -m pytest -q
```

- `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; jobs use a fresh github-hosted runner here [workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)
- requirements in this exercise are unpinned; record reviewed dependency versions for repeatable checks
- the template has no deployment step or credentials; use it to learn ci before extending the release process

## extend toward delivery

- build a versioned package or container from the checked code and approved model artifact
- record its digest, code revision, data version, and evaluation report
- staging is an environment for checking a release before production; test inference compatibility there
- apply the required approval gate, promote the same tested artifact, and retain the previous version for rollback
- run service checks after release and monitor prediction quality when outcomes arrive
- keep model selection on validation data; repeatedly tuning to a fixed test set in ci undermines its role as a final independent evaluation [ml pipeline guidance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/mlops-continuous-delivery-and-automation-pipelines-in-machine-learning)
